investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-05T19:42–19:49Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both were at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner never received a running agent and therefore produced no evidence, causing all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to be missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes. Every new remote-agent pod is immediately placed in Unschedulable state by the scheduler, with preemption also failing ("No preemption victims found"). This prevents the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885: createAgent with machineType "remote") from ever obtaining a running VM, so no evidence is written and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is entirely unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing agent pods, leaving no capacity for new probe pods. This is the most directly supported cause given the scheduler message in failed-check.message and sibling evidence.

Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the schedulable pool to those 2 already-exhausted nodes. This is a contributing structural constraint visible in the same scheduler message.

Leaked or zombie remote-agent VMs from prior eval runs consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without being cleaned up: the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1883) is intended to release resources, but if a prior run crashed before cleanup, slots may remain occupied.

Cluster under-provisioning: only 2 nodes are configured with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, which may be insufficient for concurrent eval runs or background workloads sharing the same resource pool.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is not exhausted (i.e., free slots exist on the 2 eligible nodes), the scheduling failure has a different cause such as a misconfigured resource request in the pod spec.

If the pod spec's node affinity/selector was recently changed to no longer match any node (including the 2 kata-capable nodes), the root cause would be a configuration regression rather than capacity exhaustion.

If a subsequent eval run succeeds immediately without any cluster changes, the failure was transient (e.g., a burst of concurrent workloads temporarily consumed all slots) rather than a sustained capacity problem.

If the runner's withCleanup logic is confirmed to have successfully released all prior VM slots and the cluster still shows exhaustion, the cause is insufficient total provisioned capacity rather than leaked resources.

If no pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm resources on the cluster at the time of investigation, the resource accounting or extended-resource registration on the nodes may be broken rather than the capacity being genuinely consumed.

Introduce a historical trend eval for remote-agent scheduling latency so that gradual capacity pressure (increasing unscheduled durations) is detected before full exhaustion occurs.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-05T19:42–19:49Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both were at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner never received a running agent and therefore produced no evidence, causing all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to be missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes. Every new remote-agent pod is immediately placed in Unschedulable state by the scheduler, with preemption also failing ("No preemption victims found"). This prevents the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885: createAgent with machineType "remote") from ever obtaining a running VM, so no evidence is written and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is entirely unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Kubernetes Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new pod: 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, no agent VM was provisioned, and the remote-agent-runtime eval received zero evidence — every required field (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is missing and the expected assertion ("hello from aura") could not be evaluated.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The scheduler reports "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" on those 2 nodes and "node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" on the remaining 4, leaving 0 of 6 nodes available for scheduling. Preemption was also attempted and found no victims. As a result, every remote-agent pod creation attempt timed out unscheduled (~125–149 s), preventing any agent lifecycle step from completing and producing zero eval evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or label drift on 4 of 6 nodes: those nodes are present in the cluster but are not eligible for remote-agent pods, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto only 2 nodes and making exhaustion more likely. Supported by '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' in failed-check.message.

TERTIARY — a concurrent workload spike or leaked/stuck agent pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them: if prior eval runs or user workloads did not clean up peer-pod VMs, the resource pool could be depleted. Supported circumstantially by the fact that preemption found no victims, suggesting all current occupants are non-preemptible.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — a quota or limit change on the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource that reduced the allocatable count on the 2 matching nodes. No direct evidence in the packet; would require node describe output to confirm.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is available and not exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes, the root cause is not resource exhaustion and another scheduler or admission issue must be investigated.

If the remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime checks pass on an immediate re-run without any infrastructure change, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief spike in concurrent pod creation) rather than sustained capacity exhaustion.

If the 4 non-matching nodes are found to have the correct labels and taints but the pod spec's affinity/selector was recently changed to exclude them, the primary cause shifts to a pod spec misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.

If no kata.peerpods.io/vm-consuming pods are found running on the 2 matching nodes, the resource accounting may be incorrect (e.g., a quota object or node-level limit was reduced), which would point to a configuration change rather than workload exhaustion.
If local-agent checks (local-agent-create, local-agent-runtime) are also failing at the same time, the failure scope may be broader than the remote-agent node pool.
